verdict.rationale: Grafana lets you define dashboards, data sources and other configuration as version-controllable files. Its first-party docs also say its OpenTelemetry-based collection protects against vendor lock-in and ensures data portability, and its storage backends use open Prometheus/OpenTelemetry formats with self-hostable object storage. That is real, product-owned openness, but it covers configuration and open-standard ingestion rather than a documented 'export everything and leave' path. missing for 10: a documented bulk export of stored metrics, logs and traces from Grafana Cloud, a full account or data export workflow, the export file formats, and independent or hands-on corroboration of a migration off Grafana.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: You can define data sources and dashboards using files that can be version controlled, making GitOps more natural.
This approach lets you define dashboards, data sources, and other configurations in code, enabling version control, automated testing, and reliable deployments through CI/CD pipelines.
It helps you collect metrics, logs, traces, and profiles from your applications while protecting you from vendor lock-in and ensuring data portability
provides horizontally scalable, highly available, multi-tenant, long-term storage for Prometheus and OpenTelemetry metrics.
Log data itself is then compressed and stored in chunks in object stores such as Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) or Google Cloud Storage (GCS), or even locally on the filesystem.
